c: Who am I? — The epileptic cook and illegitimate servant in a Russian landowner’s house who commits the murder everyone blames on another, then hangs himself.
Who am I? — An examining magistrate plays cat-and-mouse with a feverish student, never arresting him until the man breaks.
Who am I? — Back from a Swiss sanatorium, an epileptic and impossibly kind nobleman who walks into a Petersburg tangle of rivals and ends in silent breakdown.

A dressing gown, a sofa deep, / A landowner who’d rather sleep;
His servant Zakhar shuffles by, / While dreams of Stolz go drifting by.
Who am I? — A medical student who dissects frogs and scorns every authority, preaching nothing but usefulness until love and a typhus cut undo me.
“I am ready to love the whole world, yet nobody understands me.” A bored officer in the Caucasus wrecks every life that touches his, ending with a duel.
Who am I? — I toss a bundle of a hundred thousand rubles into a fireplace to see who will fetch it, on a birthday evening in Petersburg.
“Maman died today. Or yesterday maybe, I don’t know.” An Algiers clerk shoots a stranger on a beach because of the glare of the sun.
Who am I? — An ivory agent at the end of a river, sent up as a hero of civilization, who left his reason in the jungle with a final cry.
“I would prefer not to.” A pale copyist at a Wall Street law office gradually refuses all work, then all food.
Who am I? — A tattooed harpooneer from the island of Kokovoko who shares a bed with the narrator and later builds himself a coffin that saves another’s life.

A golf course fence, a bellowed cry, / Thirty-three years beneath the sky;
He smells like trees, he knows no clock, / And time collapses at the lock.
Who am I? — The Black cook who keeps a crumbling Mississippi household together and, on Easter Sunday, takes the idiot son to church; of us it is said we endured.
“The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it.” A languid aristocrat whose epigrams corrupt a beautiful young man’s soul.
Who am I? — A learned prisoner in the Château d’If who tunnels into a young sailor’s cell, educates him and whispers of a treasure on a Mediterranean isle.

She sold her hair, she sold her teeth, / To feed the child she had beneath;
A factory dismissed her name, / A mayor’s mercy came — too late to claim.
Who am I? — An archdeacon of Paris, alchemist and foster-father to a deformed foundling, destroyed by lust for a dancing girl.
“I think I could be a good woman if I had five thousand a year.” A penniless governess clambers up society on charm, watching Waterloo from a distance.
Who am I? — An escaped convict on the Kentish marshes frightening a small boy for a file and food, who returns years later as a secret benefactor.
Who am I? — A narrator who takes three volumes to be born, whose nose is crushed by forceps and whose life story is lost among digressions.
Who am I? — A steward fooled by a forged letter into wearing yellow stockings cross-gartered, smiling madly, and locked in a dark room.
“This island’s mine, by Sycorax my mother.” A creature of the isle curses his master with the language he was taught.

A general home from Gothic wars, / Who buried sons and settled scores;
He bakes a pie for the empress’s feast, / And serves the flesh of her sons at least.
Who am I? — A debauched landowner who once employed a young woman’s family, haunted by a dead wife, who ends with a pistol on a rainy Petersburg night.
Who am I? — A cold St. Petersburg minister whose ears and crackling knuckles his wife cannot stand, who ultimately takes in his rival’s child.
Who am I? — A dashing cavalry officer whose steeplechase fall mirrors my lover’s fate, and who ends by riding off to a war.
Who am I? — An awkward illegitimate count who inherits a vast fortune, wanders the field of Borodino, and plans to assassinate Napoleon.
“Maybe I did not live as I ought?” A judge whose pain began with a fall while hanging curtains discovers, too late, that his life was a counterfeit.
Who am I? — An exiled vivisectionist on a Pacific island who carves beasts into men in the House of Pain, and imposes a Law on them.

An asylum cell of flies and spiders, / He serves a master, sees through riders;
A lunatic with hungry stare, / He begs the Count to hear his prayer.
Who am I? — An aristocratic Styrian guest who sleepwalks through a castle at night, befriends the narrator, and is also known as Millarca.
Who am I? — A castaway abandoned on a treasure island for three years who has moved the loot.
Who am I? — A punctual clubman of Savile Row who wagers half his fortune that he can circle the globe in eighty days, and wins by an extra day gained.
Who am I? — A French manservant who has had many careers, signs on with an Englishman, rescues a widow from a pyre, and carries a pocket watch from home.
Who am I? — A blonde spy marked with a fleur-de-lis on her shoulder, who dies by the sword of a Lille executioner.
Who am I? — A musketeer who dreams of the cloth, writes poems, juggles lovers, and is eventually revealed as the head of a secret Order.

A Paris urchin, sharp and small, / He sleeps within a plaster elephant’s hall;
He sings while bullets cut the air, / Collecting cartridges there.
Who am I? — A country doctor’s wife in Yonville, undone by novels, adulteries, debts and a bottle of arsenic.
Who am I? — A carpenter’s son, tutor and seminarian who rises through two ladies’ beds and ends at the guillotine.
Who am I? — A Californian executrix who stumbles on a muted post horn symbol and a possible underground postal conspiracy called the Tristero.
Who am I? — A lieutenant who runs a syndicate in which everyone has a share, trading Egyptian cotton and even contracting to bomb his own squadron.
“What’s it going to be then, eh?” A teenage narrator who speaks Nadsat, loves Beethoven and violence, and is treated with the Ludovico technique.
Who am I? — A bespectacled asthmatic boy on a deserted island whose glasses kindle fire, and who is killed by a falling boulder as the conch shatters.
“That’s a bingo!” A polyglot SS colonel nicknamed the Jew Hunter who orders a glass of milk in a French farmhouse and savours strudel with cream.
Who am I? — A commandant who shoots prisoners from the balcony of a villa overlooking the Kraków-Płaszów camp.

A basement pit, a sewing machine, / A moth chrysalis unseen;
He stitches suits from women’s skin, / And asks the captive to lotion in.
Who am I? — The only man left in a Los Angeles overrun by blood-drinkers, who ends up as the legend of the new world, hammering stakes by day.
“Eleven hundred men went into the water.” A grizzled shark hunter on a fishing boat recounts a naval disaster in the Pacific over drinks and scars.
Who am I? — A would-be stand-up comedian who kidnaps a talk show host so that I may perform my monologue on national television.
Who am I? — A Broadway playwright holed up in a sweltering Hollywood hotel to write a wrestling picture, tormented by his neighbour.
Who am I? — A Vietnam veteran, convert to Judaism, who refuses to roll on Saturdays and brandishes a pistol over a bowling line violation.

A welder hunting in the sand, / Finds a satchel and a drug deal gone bad;
He takes the cash and hears the phone — / A stranger’s coin will claim his own.
Who am I? — Fashioned from clay by a goddess to rival a king, I lived with gazelles until a temple woman civilized me, then I fell sick for slaying a bull.
Who am I? — A Trojan princess whose true prophecies are doomed never to be believed, a curse of the sun god.
Who am I? — A blind Theban seer who lived seven years as a woman and later warned a king that he himself was the polluter of the city.

She scattered dust upon the dead, / Against a ruler’s law, she said;
Buried alive for burying kin, / A sister’s loyalty paid the sin.
Who am I? — A queen who welcomes my husband home from Troy with a purple carpet, a bath and a net, avenging our daughter.
Who am I? — A prince who kills his mother at the god’s command and is chased by the Furies until a trial on Athens’ hill acquits him.
Who am I? — A Greek archer abandoned on Lemnos with a festering snakebite, later fetched because Troy will not fall without his weapon.
Who am I? — The ugliest and most foul-mouthed soldier at Troy, a lame, bow-legged commoner who mocks kings and is beaten with a sceptre by Odysseus.

An Amazon queen who came to Troy, / To fight for Priam’s city’s joy;
Achilles struck her, then he gazed, / And wept for beauty he had razed.
Who am I? — A queen who watched fifty sons fall with her city, saw my youngest murdered by a guest, and was changed into a dog.
Who am I? — A Lycian ally of Troy and son of Zeus, who falls to Patroclus and is borne home by Sleep and Death.
Who am I? — A Norse hero who slays Fafnir, tastes his heart, and then is fatally forgotten by a ring of fire.
Who am I? — A shieldmaiden sleeping on a mountain ringed by flames, awaiting the man who can pass through, tricked into marrying another.
Who am I? — Hrothgar’s spokesman who mocks a stranger over a swimming contest, but lends him the sword Hrunting in the end.

A Christmas feast, a giant green, / A beheading game, a bargain keen;
He wears a girdle to save his skin, / And lives to bear the sash of sin.
Who am I? — Arthur’s nephew or son, who seizes the throne in his absence, then meets him at Camlann in a final fatal battle.
Who am I? — A maiden who loved Lancelot in vain, died, and drifted down a river on a barge to Camelot with a letter in her hand.
Who am I? — A paladin of Charlemagne who loses his wits over a pagan princess, and whose senses are retrieved from the moon.
Who am I? — A peasant woman of El Toboso, never seen by the reader, whom a deluded knight has made his lady.
Who am I? — A Spanish rogue who serves a blind man, a miserly priest and a starving squire, and learns survival through roguery.
“I am the spirit that always denies!” A devil who appears to a scholar in the shape of a poodle and bargains for his soul.
Who am I? — A young woman seduced by a learned doctor, who kills her newborn and refuses rescue from a prison cell.
Who am I? — A bored dandy who rejects a country girl’s letter, kills his friend in a duel, and finds her years later married to a general.

A country girl who dared to write, / And poured her heart out in the night;
She later turns her suitor down, / A princess in the capital town.
Who am I? — A genteel swindler who tours provincial Russia buying the names of dead serfs from landowners for a mortgage scheme.
Who am I? — A penniless clerk in a provincial inn who is mistaken for the inspector, and takes bribes before fleeing.
Who am I? — A pious fraud who installs himself in a rich man’s household and tries to marry his daughter and seduce his wife.
Who am I? — A Parisian nobleman who hates flattery and insists on bluntness, yet loves a coquettish widow and ends by retiring to the desert.

A general’s daughter, bored and proud, / Her father’s pistols, tightly bowed;
She burns a manuscript in flame, / And ends her story with a shot of shame.
“I must stand quite alone if I am to understand myself.” A wife dances the tarantella, then slams a door heard across Europe.
Who am I? — A Norwegian braggart who weds a troll king’s daughter, sails to Morocco, and peels an onion in search of his true core.
Who am I? — A spa town doctor who finds the baths are contaminated, and is branded by the town as an enemy of the people.
Who am I? — A disgraced banker who paces upstairs in a cold house for eight years, waiting for a call to return.
Who am I? — A canteen woman hauls a wagon across Europe in the Thirty Years’ War and loses all her children.
Who am I? — A Zenith real-estate salesman, a joiner of clubs, who briefly rebels against a conformist life and then backs down.
Who am I? — A hard-drinking salesman turned fiery evangelist who preaches against sin while indulging in all of it.

A gambler with the Series fixed, / His cufflinks strangely mixed;
He wears the molars of men, / And turns up not at the end.
Who am I? — A beautiful New York socialite whose chances for a rich marriage slip away through scandal, ending in a fatal dose of chloral.
“Tell her I’m old-fashioned.” A New York lawyer torn between his fiancée and her exiled cousin, who never goes up to her door at the end.
Who am I? — A countess who flees a European marriage to return to Old New York, scandalizing the families and haunting a lawyer’s dreams.
Who am I? — The stable buck who lives apart in a room by the barn, with books and a bad back, and is allowed one conversation with dreamers.
“Wherever there’s a cop beating a guy, I’ll be there.” A parolee who returns to a dust-bowl farm and joins a family’s westward trek.
Who am I? — A former preacher who lost his faith but found a bigger sense of the holy in people, and dies defending strikers.
Who am I? — A Quaker first mate who objects to a captain’s revenge and contemplates killing him as he sleeps, but is too principled.
Who am I? — A handsome young sailor with a stutter who strikes a superior dead with one blow and is hanged from a yardarm.

A master-at-arms with a pallid face, / Who hates the boy’s sunny grace;
He lies about mutiny, and then / Is struck down dead before the men.
Who am I? — A malicious, grinning dwarf and moneylender who torments an old man and his granddaughter, drowning in the Thames.
“Something will turn up.” A perpetually debt-ridden optimist who finally exposes a villainous clerk before sailing to Australia.
Who am I? — A Little Britain lawyer who washes his hands after cross-examining clients and keeps a housekeeper with scarred wrists.
Who am I? — A sullen, rich, lumbering rival nicknamed after an arachnid, who marries and mistreats a heroine and is killed by a horse.

A burglar with a pit-bull friend, / Whose temper brings a girl to end;
He flees across the rooftops dark, / And hangs himself, caught in the dark.
Who am I? — A dissolute barrister who resembles a French émigré and takes his place in a prison cell on the eve of the guillotine.
Who am I? — A Paris wine-shop keeper who knits the names of the condemned into her stitches.
Who am I? — A cockney bootblack turned manservant to a club president, famed for comparisons that begin with a saying and end with a pun.
Who am I? — A dim dragoon guardsman who loves his wife and horse and finally discovers her intimacy with a marquis.
Who am I? — A wealthy, wicked marquis who protects a social climber and leaves her ruined when her husband returns.
Who am I? — An Irish rogue who elopes, deserts, gambles across Europe, marries a rich widow and loses it all.
Who am I? — A big-game hunter, ex-colonel, and chief of staff to a consulting criminal, felled by an air gun across the street from Baker Street.
Who am I? — A bearded, bellowing scientist who leads an expedition to a South American plateau of surviving dinosaurs.

A hunter old with elephant gun, / A hidden mine, a vanished son;
With Sir Henry and Good they go, / Through Kukuanaland’s deadly show.
Who am I? — A hesitant Royal Navy midshipman who becomes an admiral, anxious and seasick, always hiding his doubts behind duty.
Who am I? — An Anglo-Irish physician, naturalist, intelligence agent and cello player, friend of a sea captain.
Who am I? — A rumpled spymaster with thick glasses and a faithless wife, who hunts a Soviet rival through the Circus.
Who am I? — A burnt-out British agent who pretends to defect in order to ruin an East German intelligence officer and dies at the Berlin Wall.

A cabaret in Weimar days, / Green-painted nails and daring ways;
She sings and drinks on Berlin nights, / While brown shirts gather in the lights.
Who am I? — A painter who revisits a great English estate during wartime and recalls his friendship with a charming, drunken undergraduate.
Who am I? — An Oxford aristocrat with a teddy bear called Aloysius, fleeing his family to a Moroccan monastery.
Who am I? — A renowned German writer who travels to the Lido, becomes obsessed with a beautiful Polish boy, and lingers while cholera spreads.
